messages:
Maya: Hi all, first day! Trying to get my dev env working on Ubuntu 22.04. Followed the quickstart but I'm stuck: installed Homebrew (Linuxbrew) into ~/.linuxbrew, installed asdf via the distro package, added the asdf init to .zshrc, but when I open a non-login VSCode terminal the `node` shim isn't found. `which asdf` returns /usr/bin/asdf, but `asdf where` is empty in the VSCode terminal. Any pointers?

Priya: welcome, Maya! Common cause is shell startup files differences between login and non-login shells. VSCode's integrated terminal defaults to a non-login interactive shell. For zsh we usually add the asdf init to both ~/.zprofile and ~/.zshrc. Put this in ~/.zprofile so login shells and GUI-launched apps inherit PATH: `source /usr/share/asdf/asdf.sh` (or wherever asdf is). Then in ~/.zshrc add `source /usr/share/asdf/completions/asdf.zsh` and `eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"` if you use direnv.

Sam: also check your PATH ordering. If you installed Homebrew in ~/.linuxbrew, ensure `export PATH="$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin:$HOME/.linuxbrew/sbin:$PATH"` is in ~/.profile or ~/.zprofile. VSCode might spawn the shell without reading ~/.profile; you can tell the Remote extension to run a login shell in settings (terminal.integrated.inheritEnv / shellArgs).

Maya: ah ok. I had PATH in ~/.bashrc leftover from another guide. Moved the brew export to ~/.zprofile and added the asdf source there, restarted VSCode and now `asdf where nodejs` shows the correct path but `node -v` is still system node 10.

Priya: After installing a runtime with asdf you need to `asdf global nodejs 18.16.0` (or local) and run `asdf reshim`. The shims directory must be first in PATH. Add `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"` to ~/.zprofile before the brew path. On Linux, if asdf is installed system-wide, the shims location might be /usr/share/asdf/shims.

Sam: minor but helpful: some distro packages install asdf under /usr/lib/asdf which expects shims under /usr/lib/asdf/shims. `asdf where` and `asdf current` will clarify. Also run `type -a node` to see which binary is being picked.

Maya: Ran `type -a node` and it shows `/usr/bin/node` then `/home/maya/.asdf/shims/node`. So PATH ordering is still wrong. I moved the shims export higher and restarted, now node from asdf is first. Thanks.

Priya: Nice. Two other heads-ups: 1) building some packages (python, ruby) requires brew libs (openssl, libffi). For example for python build I had to set `export LDFLAGS="-L$HOME/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I$HOME/.linuxbrew/opt/openssl/include"` before `asdf install python 3.11.4`. 2) If you use direnv, make sure the envrc exposes those flags or they won't load in the project shell.

Maya: I'm also trying to wire 1Password SSH keys for git. In the devcontainer the ssh agent forwarding seems flaky. Any recommended approach?

Sam: For devcontainers we put a small helper under dotfiles: `scripts/start-ssh-with-op` that signs you in and adds the key into a persistent ssh-agent socket the container mounts. The general flow is `eval "$(op signin --sh)"` then `op item get <ssh-key> --attributes privateKey | ssh-add -` . If you prefer the 1Password native SSH integration, you can follow their setup but it requires a GUI agent.

Priya: Onboarding note: if using VSCode Remote - Containers, add `remoteUser: "vscode"` and mount the ssh-agent socket via `mounts` in devcontainer.json. We document this in the dotfiles README: https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles#devcontainer-ssh.

Maya: Good to know. One last question: some of my project builds expect `GEM_HOME` or `PYENV_ROOT`. Should I set those globally or via direnv per project?

Sam: Prefer direnv per-project so you don't pollute global envs. Example .envrc snippets we use: `export PYENV_ROOT="$HOME/.pyenv"` (only if using pyenv) or `export GEM_HOME="$HOME/.gem"` and then `source_env $REPO_ROOT/.envrc` if shared. For asdf-managed runtimes you usually don't need PYENV_ROOT unless mixing tools. Keep the LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS in .envrc if build deps live in brew.

Maya: Thanks everyone! Followed Priya's zprofile + shims ordering fix, set LDFLAGS for python, and I'll try the dotfiles helper for ssh. Appreciated :slightly_smiling_face:
